```plato
//==
// # Triangulation
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Rings over a point pool
//  - Nodes and the node buffer
//  - Ring construction and cleanup
//  - Hole bridging
//  - Ear clipping
//  - The IMesh2D obligations

library Triangulation
{
    //==
    // # Rings over a point pool
    //
    // Every triangulation here works over one POOL of points and a set of RINGS
    // naming slices of it: ring 0 is the outer boundary and ring r > 0 is the hole
    // starting at `holeStarts[r - 1]`, each running to the next start (the last to
    // the end of the pool). Faces come back as `TriangleFace` over pool indices, so
    // a result always points back at the vertices it was built from.
    //
    // Conventions fixed here:
    //
    //   * WINDING: the outer ring is made counter-clockwise and every hole
    //     clockwise, whatever winding the caller stored. Ear clipping below assumes
    //     it. Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding.
    //   * Coincidence is tested EXACTLY, never with a tolerance: a bridged ring
    //     contains deliberately duplicated vertices, and a tolerance would also
    //     merge distinct nearby vertices of a finely sampled ring.
    //   * A ring reduced below three vertices by cleanup encloses nothing and is
    //     dropped rather than triangulated.

    // The number of rings: the boundary plus one per hole.
    RingCount(holeStarts: Array<Integer>): Integer
        => holeStarts.Count + 1;

    // Where ring `r` starts in the pool.
    RingStart(holeStarts: Array<Integer>, r: Integer): Integer
        => r == 0 ? 0 : holeStarts[r - 1];

    // Where ring `r` ends in the pool, exclusive.
    RingEnd(holeStarts: Array<Integer>, r: Integer, poolCount: Integer): Integer
        => r == holeStarts.Count ? poolCount : holeStarts[r];

    // The signed area of the pool points in [start, end) taken in stored order:
    // positive when they wind counter-clockwise.
    RangeSignedArea(points: Array<Point2D>, start: Integer, end: Integer): Number
        => points.Slice(start, end).ShoelaceArea;

    // True when `a` precedes `b` in the left-to-right, then bottom-to-top order the
    // bridge search scans in. A strict total order on distinct points.
    IsFurtherLeft(a: Point2D, b: Point2D): Boolean
        => a.X < b.X || (a.X == b.X && a.Y < b.Y);

    // True when the two points are exactly coincident.
    IsSamePoint(a: Point2D, b: Point2D): Boolean
        => a.X == b.X && a.Y == b.Y;

    // The leftmost of the pool points in [start, end). Precondition: non-empty.
    LeftmostOfRange(points: Array<Point2D>, start: Integer, end: Integer): Point2D
        => points.Slice(start, end)
            .Reduce(points[start], (best, p) => p.IsFurtherLeft(best) ? p : best);

    // True when hole `g` is bridged before hole `h`, given `h`'s leftmost vertex.
    PrecedesHole(holeStarts: Array<Integer>, points: Array<Point2D>, g: Integer,
        h: Integer, leftmostOfH: Point2D): Boolean
    {
        var theirs = points.LeftmostOfRange(holeStarts.RingStart(g + 1),
            holeStarts.RingEnd(g + 1, points.Count));
        return theirs.IsFurtherLeft(leftmostOfH)
            || (theirs.IsSamePoint(leftmostOfH) && g < h);
    }

    // The number of holes that must be bridged before hole `h`: those whose
    // leftmost vertex lies further left, with the stored order breaking ties.
    HolesBefore(points: Array<Point2D>, holeStarts: Array<Integer>, h: Integer): Integer
    {
        var mine = points.LeftmostOfRange(holeStarts.RingStart(h + 1),
            holeStarts.RingEnd(h + 1, points.Count));
        return holeStarts.Count.Range.Reduce(0, (count, g) => count
            + (holeStarts.PrecedesHole(points, g, h, mine) ? 1 : 0));
    }

    // The holes in the order they must be bridged: left to right, so that a bridge
    // never has to cross a hole that is still separate. Sorted by rank rather than
    // by comparison, which needs no scratch storage.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon_triangulation#Ear_clipping_method
    HolesLeftToRight(points: Array<Point2D>, holeStarts: Array<Integer>): Array<Integer>
        => holeStarts.Count.MapRange(rank => holeStarts.Count.Range
            .Reduce(0, (found, h) => points.HolesBefore(holeStarts, h) == rank ? h : found));

    //==
    // # Nodes and the node buffer
    //
    // The rings live in one affine `Buffer<EarClipNode>` as an indexed circular
    // doubly-linked list: unlinking a clipped ear is O(1) and needs no array
    // rebuilding. The buffer is the affine object; the nodes in it are ordinary
    // values, so the updates below return copies and the caller writes them back.
    // Slots [0, poolCount) mirror the pool one for one; the two slots each hole
    // bridge needs sit above them.
    //
    // PARAMETER ORDER: the buffer is never the FIRST parameter of a function
    // declared here. The C# writer plans an extension surface per concrete type and
    // skips `unique` types (`Plato.CSharpWriter/CSharpWriter.cs:68`), so a function
    // dispatching on `Buffer<T>` is silently dropped from the emitted code while its
    // call sites survive — the generated C# then does not compile. Every function
    // below therefore leads with the point pool or with the slot it works on, and
    // takes the buffer second. Tracked as plato-416.

    // The node with a new predecessor.
    WithPrev(n: EarClipNode, prev: Integer): EarClipNode
        => EarClipNode(n.Vertex, prev, n.Next, n.Active);

    // The node with a new successor.
    WithNext(n: EarClipNode, next: Integer): EarClipNode
        => EarClipNode(n.Vertex, n.Prev, next, n.Active);

    // The node marked dead. Its links are kept so a walk already standing on it can
    // still step off.
    Removed(n: EarClipNode): EarClipNode
        => EarClipNode(n.Vertex, n.Prev, n.Next, false);

    // The pool point the node at `slot` names.
    NodePoint(points: Array<Point2D>, nodes: Buffer<EarClipNode>, slot: Integer): Point2D
        => points[nodes.At(slot).Vertex.Value];

    // Twice the signed area of the corner at `slot`: positive when it turns
    // counter-clockwise, which in a counter-clockwise ring means convex; zero when
    // its two edges are collinear.
    CornerTurn(points: Array<Point2D>, nodes: Buffer<EarClipNode>, slot: Integer): Number
        => TwiceSignedArea(
            points.NodePoint(nodes, nodes.At(slot).Prev),
            points.NodePoint(nodes, slot),
            points.NodePoint(nodes, nodes.At(slot).Next));

    // True when the vertex at `slot` lies in the triangle (a, b, c) without being
    // one of its corners — the test that disqualifies an ear.
    BlocksEar(points: Array<Point2D>, nodes: Buffer<EarClipNode>, slot: Integer,
        a: Integer, b: Integer, c: Integer): Boolean
    {
        var q = points.NodePoint(nodes, slot);
        var pa = points.NodePoint(nodes, a);
        var pb = points.NodePoint(nodes, b);
        var pc = points.NodePoint(nodes, c);
        return q.IsSamePoint(pa).Not && q.IsSamePoint(pb).Not && q.IsSamePoint(pc).Not
            && Triangle2D(pa, pb, pc).Contains(q);
    }
```
